mood.p: Zondag verloopt wisselvallig met buien die over het land trekken, vooral langs de kust, en tussendoor zonnige perioden bij 20 tot 21 graden aan zee en rond 23 graden in het oosten. Daarmee sluit een opvallend warme en droge augustusmaand af, volgens Weeronline de op zeven na warmste ooit in De Bilt gemeten. De stemming in het land is gemengd: de steekpartij op Amsterdam Centraal en de verloren WK-hockeyfinale drukken op het weekend, terwijl Den Haag zich opmaakt voor de laatste ronde begrotingsonderhandelingen voor Prinsjesdag.

global.h3: Russian drone hits Ukrainian arms depot, killing 37 near Kyiv
global.summary: A Russian drone strike on an ammunition warehouse in the village of Myla set off hours of explosions, killing at least 37 people in the deadliest attack in the Kyiv region this year.
body: A Russian drone attack late on Friday hit an ammunition warehouse at Myla, west of Kyiv, triggering a large fire and waves of secondary detonations that lasted for hours in a residential area. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said at least 37 people were killed, dozens were wounded and hundreds were evacuated.

Nearby buildings including homes and a facility for elderly people and people with disabilities suffered heavy damage. Zelenskyy said he would pursue accountability for suspected negligence in how the munitions were stored, noting this was the second such incident in two months after a strike on a warehouse at Vyshneve killed seven people.

global.h3: Ukraine downs 233 drones as air raid alerts run into third day
global.summary: Ukrainian air defences reported shooting down or suppressing 233 Russian drones overnight, while Kyiv said its own units struck Russian military and logistics targets.
body: Ukraine's military said air defences destroyed or jammed 233 Russian drones across northern, southern, eastern and central regions overnight into 29 August. Drones continued to target Kyiv and its surroundings into the morning, extending an unusually long stretch of rolling air raid alerts.

Ukraine's General Staff said its forces struck Russian drone sites and command posts in occupied territory during the same night. Several locations in Russia's Rostov region were also reported as targets, along with a logistics warehouse.

global.h3: Niger junta says army mutiny in Niamey has been contained
global.summary: Gunfire and explosions rocked the Nigerien capital overnight as soldiers moved against the ruling junta, in the first serious internal challenge since the 2023 coup.
body: Sustained gunfire and blasts were heard overnight into Saturday around Niamey's main airport, which houses the Base 101 military facility, and in the Plateau district where the presidential palace and key state institutions sit. State broadcaster RTN later said the situation was under control.

Authorities said mutinous soldiers had detained some of their colleagues at a military base and fired on sites in the capital. State media reported that dozens of the rebelling soldiers were arrested or killed.

global.h3: Iran says it holds Hormuz and is in no hurry to reopen it
global.summary: Tehran insisted the Strait of Hormuz remains closed six months into the war with the United States and Israel, while US Central Command disputed Iran's claim of control.
body: Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the Strait of Hormuz remains shut and that Tehran is in no rush to reopen it. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it maintains firm control of the waterway and accused US officials of misleading statements aimed at moving energy prices.

US Central Command, which is enforcing a blockade of Iranian ports, rejected that account and said Iran does not control the strait. President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iranian exports have fallen by close to 35 percent under sanctions and the naval blockade.

global.h3: Settlers seize Palestinian home in Qusra as West Bank violence spreads
global.summary: Dozens of Israeli settlers took over a house in the West Bank village of Qusra with the family still inside, one of several attacks that wounded at least five Palestinians.
body: Extremist settlers attacked Qusra, southeast of Nablus, on Saturday and occupied a Palestinian home while the family was inside. The military was called to remove them. A Palestinian woman was injured and taken to hospital, one of at least five Palestinians hurt in settler attacks across the West Bank that day.

No arrests appeared to have been made by late Saturday, and residents said Israeli troops fired tear gas at Palestinians. Qusra has faced a wave of settler attacks in recent weeks, including a prolonged siege on several homes.

global.h3: Gaza truce frays as Israeli strike kills Hamas commander
global.summary: Israel said it killed a Hamas commander in Deir al-Balah, days after the US envoy running the ceasefire effort warned the deal is close to a point of no return.
body: The Israeli military said it struck and killed a Hamas commander who was hiding next to Shuhada al-Aqsa Hospital in the Deir al-Balah area, arguing the operatives were preparing attacks and rebuilding Hamas capabilities in breach of the ceasefire. Several people were wounded in a separate Israeli air strike in central Gaza on Sunday.
Gaza's health ministry says at least 1,313 Palestinians have been killed since the truce took effect in October, even as the heaviest fighting has subsided.

global.h3: US, South Korea and Japan confirm Freedom Edge drill off Jeju
global.summary: Seoul said the trilateral Freedom Edge exercise will begin on 7 September for five days, a day after Pyongyang vowed to retaliate against what it called US hostility.
body: South Korea's military said the three countries will press ahead with Freedom Edge in waters off Jeju Island, starting 7 September and running for five days. The announcement followed a North Korean threat to retaliate over US actions.

Launched in 2024, Freedom Edge combines simultaneous air and naval drills covering ballistic missile defence, anti submarine warfare and surveillance. Pyongyang has previously called it a reckless show of strength.

global.h3: Russia test fires Yars intercontinental missile from Plesetsk
global.summary: Moscow's defence ministry said a mobile Yars ICBM launched from Plesetsk delivered its warheads to the Kura range in Kamchatka, days after the CIA chief visited Russia.
body: The Russian Ministry of Defence said the nuclear capable Yars missile was fired from the Plesetsk test site and that all warheads reached the Kura range in Kamchatka. The stated purpose was to confirm the flight and technical characteristics of the system.

Footage released by the ministry showed the launch taking place from a shelter, with the missile brought to the site from a remote deployment base. The previous Yars launch was in May 2026 during a strategic forces exercise.

global.h3: Israel strikes multiple sites across southern Lebanon
global.summary: Israeli aircraft, artillery and a drone hit several locations in the Nabatieh district on Saturday, extending a sharp escalation in strikes on south Lebanon.
body: A Lebanese military source said Israeli aircraft struck al-Deir and Ali al Taher Hill, artillery shelled Haris and Haddatha, and a drone fired on Nabih Berri Avenue in Nabatieh city. A large explosion was reported in the south following the strikes.
The bombardment follows a wave of Israeli attacks on 15 August that Lebanon said killed 11 people including several children.

global.h3: CIA chief floated Trump, Putin and Zelenskyy summit in Moscow
global.summary: John Ratcliffe proposed a three way leaders meeting during a secret trip to Moscow this week, according to sources briefed on the talks.
body: Ratcliffe travelled clandestinely to Moscow on Tuesday and met Sergei Naryshkin, head of Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service, and FSB Director Alexander Bortnikov. One aim was to test whether Russian intelligence chiefs could push Vladimir Putin toward resuming US mediated talks with Ukraine.
During the meetings Ratcliffe delivered a pessimistic assessment of how the fighting is going for Russian forces and concluded that Bortnikov could be a constructive player in reviving diplomacy.

global.h3: Trump announces US control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil
global.summary: Washington said it secured majority control of a joint venture holding a 100 year concession over Venezuelan fields containing more than 65 billion barrels of reserves.
body: Trump announced on Friday evening that the United States had struck a deal giving it majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of proven Venezuelan reserves, calling it the biggest oil deal in world history and saying it came at no cost to US taxpayers.

Interim Venezuelan president Delcy Rodriguez granted a private joint venture a 100 year concession over the fields. The US government will hold 55 percent of the venture, split between equity and the right to buy oil at cost. Rodriguez called the agreement a historic milestone and projected more than 100 billion dollars in investment.

global.h3: Canada answers Lake Ontario renaming with a giant lakeside sign
global.summary: Ottawa installed a large sign reading Lake Ontario now and always after Trump signed an order renaming the lake Lake America amid a deepening trade war.
body: Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario as Lake America, effective immediately, after trade talks with Canada collapsed. The US Geological Survey has already applied the change across official documents, with printed material to follow over the coming days.

Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada will not adopt the new name and gave a short history lesson, noting the name is more than 400 years old and comes from the Wendat word Ontari'io, meaning the lake is beautiful and big. Canada's own geographic names database still lists Lake Ontario.

global.h3: Khamenei urges Gulf rulers to identify their real enemy
global.summary: Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei used a written message for Islamic Unity Week to call on Muslim states, especially Gulf governments, to close ranks.
body: The message, published on Khamenei's Telegram account to mark Islamic Unity Week and the birthday of the Prophet Muhammad, urged rulers of Islamic countries and particularly those in West Asia and the Gulf to identify their real enemy, understand its plan and confront it.

Khamenei argued that anyone who sows division among Muslims, knowingly or not, serves the enemies of Islam. He accused the United States and Israel of exploiting racial, cultural, social, political and geographical differences to weaken the Muslim world.

global.h3: Norway's King Harald V dies at 89, son becomes King Haakon VIII
global.summary: Europe's oldest reigning monarch died in Oslo after 35 years on the throne and was immediately succeeded by his son.
body: King Harald V died on 28 August at Oslo University Hospital Rikshospitalet at the age of 89. He had been in hospital since 17 August. His son succeeded him at once as King Haakon VIII.

Harald became king on 17 January 1991 at the age of 53 after the death of his father Olav V. As a child he went into exile in the United States during the Nazi occupation of Norway, and he was widely credited with modernising the monarchy.

global.h3: Gandalf protesters target Peter Thiel's influence in Argentina
global.summary: Demonstrators in wizard costumes have marched on the billionaire's Buenos Aires mansion over his energy investment and Palantir's reach in the country.
body: Protesters calling themselves Ciudadan@s Gandalf gathered outside Thiel's home in the wealthy Palermo Chico district carrying a banner reading you shall not pass. The costume theme plays on Palantir, the data company Thiel co-founded, which takes its name from Tolkien's seeing stones.

According to Argentine outlet Infocielo, the group objected to Thiel's 76 million dollar investment in Vista Energy, an oil producer operating in northern Patagonia. Palantir holds government contracts for predictive policing, border control and military intelligence in several countries, raising civil liberties concerns in Argentina.

global.h3: Nepal and Tibet flood toll passes 750 with over 3,000 missing
global.summary: Four days after flash floods tore through the Trishuli valley and the China border zone, the confirmed death toll has climbed sharply and thousands remain unaccounted for.
body: Flash floods and mudslides struck on the morning of 26 August along a 72 kilometre stretch of the Trishuli River, hitting settlements across Nepal's Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, Tanahun, Nawalparasi and Chitwan districts. The Gyirong Port complex on the China and Nepal border, the main gateway for trade and tourism between the two countries, was destroyed.

Confirmed deaths across Nepal and the Tibet region reached 750, with Nepal's disaster agency reporting 734 dead and Chinese authorities confirming at least 16 in Tibet. More than 3,000 people are still missing, including at least 2,498 in Nepal of whom 589 are foreign nationals, and 546 in Tibet including at least 261 foreigners.

global.h3: Families hunt for pilgrims lost in the Nepal Tibet floods
global.summary: Hundreds of foreign nationals travelling to Mount Kailash are among the missing, including 33 Britons, as relatives press governments for information.
body: Many of those swept away were pilgrims heading through Nepal to Mount Kailash, a Hindu holy site in China's Tibet region. Nepal's tourism board said 33 British citizens are among the missing, and a Hindu priest is among them.

Indians make up the largest group of foreigners unaccounted for, followed by Australians, Americans, Britons, Canadians, Malaysians, South Koreans and Japanese. At one stage rescuers were searching for nearly 1,500 people including more than 700 foreigners.

global.h3: Around 6,000 seafarers still trapped in the Gulf after six months
global.summary: The UN maritime agency says roughly 400 ships and their crews remain stuck inside the Persian Gulf, unable to transit a Strait of Hormuz largely closed by the war.
body: IMO Secretary General Arsenio Dominguez said about 6,000 seafarers aboard some 400 vessels are still stranded six months after the conflict between the United States, Israel and Iran began. That is down from an estimated 20,000 seafarers on 2,000 ships at the peak.

The IMO has verified at least 70 attacks on international shipping since the war started, and says 19 seafarers have been killed. The crews come mainly from India and the Philippines, with others from Bangladesh, Pakistan, Syria and Ukraine.

global.h3: Spain asks Frontex for help with 5,000 migrants stuck in Ceuta
global.summary: Madrid requested EU border agency support to process migrants still in the enclave a month after a record mass crossing, as local protests turn violent.
body: Spain asked the European Border and Coast Guard Agency for help processing around 5,000 migrants who remain in Ceuta a month after crossing from Morocco. Spanish authorities said 69,500 migrants had already been returned to Morocco and described those returns as voluntary.
More than 70,000 people crossed into the North African territory without authorisation at the end of July in the largest mass migration Ceuta has seen. At least 72 died attempting the journey.

global.h3: UN warns Gaza hunger will worsen despite record aid deliveries
global.summary: Aid agencies reached more than 600,000 people with food in August, but the IPC projects 1.4 million Gazans in crisis level hunger or worse by December.
body: UN partners distributed food parcels and wheat flour to more than 600,000 people during the August cycle, collecting hundreds of pallets of supplies from the Kerem Shalom crossing including fruit, vegetables, adult diapers, school supplies and fuel.
Food security had improved after the October 2025 ceasefire opened up access and reduced the intensity of fighting. That progress is now judged fragile.

netherlands.h3: Coalition resumes budget talks without a Kamer majority
netherlands.summary: D66, VVD and CDA return to the table on Sunday to finish a budget that still has no majority behind it, with the Council of State deadline on Tuesday.
body: The three coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA picked up their budget negotiations again on Sunday, with parts of the package still to be written up. Talks ran on until early Friday evening.

After roughly two weeks of discussions with opposition parties, the minority cabinet has to settle on a budget among themselves first. Prime Minister Rob Jetten said on Friday that there is still time to negotiate with the opposition before the deadline.

netherlands.h3: Minister apologises for abuse in closed youth care
netherlands.summary: Long-Term Care Minister Mirjam Sterk apologised to victims of abuse in closed youth institutions and pledged to end the practice. Care bodies call it only a first step.
body: Speaking at the Akoesticum in Ede on Saturday, Minister of Long-Term Care Mirjam Sterk of the CDA apologised to people who suffered physical, mental and in some cases sexual abuse in closed youth care institutions. She said the state had failed to offer a safe place and good care, and described a strict and oppressive living environment in which many experienced violence.

The case centres on the lack of adequate compensation for victims, in particular within the very intensive short-term observation and stabilisation units known as ZIKOS. Former residents describe degrading treatment, being restrained and long periods of isolation.

netherlands.h3: Wind turbines must stand twice as far from homes as blade tips
netherlands.summary: The government set a fixed setback rule for wind turbines. Sector body NedZero says it will take more turbines to generate the same power.
body: The government has ruled that wind turbines must be sited at a distance from homes equal to twice the height of their blade tips. Wind energy trade association NedZero says the effect is that more turbines will be needed to produce the same amount of electricity.

NedZero argues a fixed national standard makes little sense because every location differs. Chairman Jan Vos said turbines can be installed in many places without causing nuisance and urged the cabinet to set out grounds for exemption quickly.

netherlands.h3: The Hague orders Extinction Rebellion off the A12
netherlands.summary: Mayor Jan van Zanen told climate activists to clear the Utrechtsebaan on Saturday. Two people were arrested as a new hard line on motorway blockades takes effect.
body: Extinction Rebellion activists walked onto the Utrechtsebaan section of the A12 in The Hague from the off-ramps at around 1pm on Saturday, causing tailbacks for drivers leaving the city. Mayor Jan van Zanen ordered them to clear the road or be removed.

Two protesters were arrested for refusing to leave, with the arrests coming shortly before police issued the order to vacate, ANP reported. An XR spokesperson told NOS that protesting on a motorway is not forbidden and that any charges would be challenged in court.

netherlands.h3: Fines agency pulls website offline after data mix-up
netherlands.summary: The CJIB shut down its digital services after a technical fault linked offences to the wrong people and allowed some users to see other individuals' records.
body: The Central Judicial Collection Agency, the body that collects court-ordered payments including traffic fines, said on Saturday it had taken its online system offline after a technical fault linked violations and offences to the wrong individuals.

People have been unable to log in to the CJIB digital system since Friday, when the problem was first spotted. Users who were already logged in were able to view other people's information before the site was shut down.

netherlands.h3: Police confirm arson attempt at Valkenswaard asylum site
netherlands.summary: Investigators established that someone deliberately tried to set fire to a building approved to house 40 unaccompanied minors in Brabant.
body: Police have confirmed that a fire was deliberately set at a building on the Leenderweg in Valkenswaard, Noord-Brabant, that had been approved as a future reception centre for asylum seekers. Officers had already suspected arson after reports of soot and broken windows. The extent of the damage is not yet clear.
The Central Agency for the Reception of Asylum Seekers signed off on the plans about a week and a half earlier. The centre is due to house around 40 unaccompanied minors.

netherlands.h3: Rotterdam port strike raises reliability worries
netherlands.summary: Unions FNV and CNV have called a stoppage for 4 September. A port economist says the bigger risk is to Rotterdam's reputation rather than the day itself.
body: FNV and CNV have asked dockworkers in Rotterdam, Amsterdam and Zeeland to stop work from 11.15am to 7pm on Friday 4 September as part of a wider campaign against government social security plans.

Port economist Bart Kuipers of Erasmus University Rotterdam said the short stoppage is unlikely to cause major immediate damage because it was announced well in advance and disruptions of a few hours are not unusual. His larger concern is reputational, as reliability weighs increasingly heavily when container lines choose ports.

netherlands.h3: Drought cuts Dutch harvests by 10 to 30 percent
netherlands.summary: Arable farmers are bringing in far less food than normal after a dry summer, with smaller carrots, onions and potatoes and lighter lettuce heads.
body: Farmers are harvesting on average 10 to 30 percent less than normal because of the drought, Andre Hoogendijk of arable sector knowledge centre BO Akkerbouw told Trouw. Carrots, onions and potatoes from the summer crop are smaller, lettuce heads are lighter and some broccoli has grown into unusual shapes.
Growers who were barred from irrigating in recent months have been hit hardest, Hoogendijk said, especially on the sandy soils of the east and south.

netherlands.h3: Beer excise pushes Dutch shoppers across the border
netherlands.summary: Brewers say beer sales in border regions have fallen 4 percent more sharply than elsewhere since the 2024 excise rise, with another increase expected in 2027.
body: More people in the Netherlands are choosing to buy cheaper beer across the border, trade association Nederlandse Brouwers said, citing research by Circana. A crate typically costs a couple of euros less in neighbouring countries.

Since the excise duty increase in 2024, beer sales in Dutch border regions have dropped 4 percent more sharply than in the rest of the country. The sector says overall Dutch beer sales are falling partly because of the high duty.

netherlands.h3: Six in ten student rooms advertised above the legal cap
netherlands.summary: An Argos analysis of 2,637 Kamernet ads found rooms priced an average of 239 euros a month over the maximum, rising above 400 euros in Amsterdam.
body: Investigative programme Argos compared the advertised rent on 2,637 listings on Kamernet, the largest Dutch rental platform, against the legal maximum each room may charge. Six in ten rooms advertised over July and August were priced above the cap, on average 239 euros a month too high.
In Amsterdam, where the average room costs close to 1,000 euros a month, 97 percent of sampled rooms exceeded the cap by an average of 421 euros. In Utrecht the share was 72 percent.

netherlands.h3: Four injured in stabbing at Amsterdam Centraal
netherlands.summary: Emergency services responded at around 7.30pm on Saturday. The suspect was among the injured and was arrested after treatment in hospital.
body: Four people were hurt in a stabbing at Amsterdam Centraal station on Saturday evening, NOS reported. Emergency services were called at around 7.30pm.

The suspect was among the injured and was arrested by police after first being taken to hospital. One other victim was also hospitalised. Police told NU.nl the severity of the injuries is unclear but that they are at least not life threatening.

netherlands.h3: August closes as eighth warmest on the Dutch record
netherlands.summary: De Bilt hit 20C or more on 30 of 31 days. Rainfall came in at 67mm against a normal 88mm, deepening a summer drought.
body: Weather service Weeronline reports that this August was the eighth warmest on the Dutch record. Temperatures in De Bilt, where measurements are taken, reached 20C or higher on 30 of the month's 31 days.

The single exception was 19 August, when the maximum stopped at 19.7C and ended a record run of 64 warm days. On 13 August De Bilt set a date record of 33.1C and Maastricht reached 36.1C, while the following day Westdorpe hit 37.7C.

netherlands.h3: Mass sperm donor says he fathered at least 199 children
netherlands.summary: In a letter to parents obtained by Nieuwsuur, the 43-year-old Groningen donor revised his own count sharply upwards from the 121 reported this week.
body: A Dutch mass sperm donor known as Simon wrote in a letter to parents, obtained by Nieuwsuur, that he has fathered at least 199 children rather than the 121 previously reported.

The 43-year-old set out where the children live: 172 in the Netherlands, 15 in Germany, 11 in Belgium and one in an undisclosed European country. He said one woman is currently pregnant with another child.

netherlands.h3: Argentina beat Oranje in hockey World Cup final shoot-out
netherlands.summary: The Dutch women missed out on a fourth straight world title after a 1-1 draw at the Wagener Stadium was settled from the spot.
body: Argentina denied the Netherlands a fourth consecutive women's hockey World Cup title on Saturday, winning the final on shoot-outs at the Wagener Stadium after the sides finished level at 1-1.

Yibbi Jansen put Oranje ahead from a penalty corner shortly before half time. Argentina pushed hard after the break and earned eight penalty corners in total before Maria Granatto levelled in the fourth quarter.
